subject: AI & Agents
title: Perceptrons: The First Neural Network
description: Learn Perceptrons: The First Neural Network in one minute.

hook.text: In 1958, the New York Times reported a machine that could learn. The hype was enormous.

buildup.text: Frank Rosenblatt built the perceptron — a single-layer neural network inspired by brain cells.

discovery.text: It could learn to classify simple patterns: separating circles from squares.

twist.text: In 1969, Minsky and Papert proved perceptrons couldn't handle XOR — a basic logic problem.

climax.text: Neural network research froze for over a decade. The proof was devastating.

punchline.text: One limitation killed a decade of progress.

details.summary: Frank Rosenblatt's perceptron in 1958 was the first neural network that could learn from data. It simulated a simplified neuron, adjusting its connections to classify simple patterns.
details.whyItMatters: The perceptron introduced the principle that machines could learn rather than being explicitly programmed. Despite early limitations, this idea became the foundation of all modern deep learning.
takeaways: The perceptron was the first learning neural network model
It adjusted connection weights to improve pattern classification
The learning principle underpins all modern neural networks

faq.question: What could the original perceptron do?
faq.answer: It could learn to classify simple visual patterns, like distinguishing shapes. It adjusted numerical weights on its inputs based on errors, gradually improving its accuracy — the first demonstration of machine learning.

faq.question: Why was the perceptron initially controversial?
faq.answer: Minsky and Papert proved single-layer perceptrons could not solve problems like XOR. This criticism dampened neural network research for over a decade, contributing to the first AI winter.
